channel.description: Latest articles from The Berkshire Edge (theberkshireedge.com)

item.title: World Tuberculosis Day is March 24 - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: We can identify, treat, and cure tuberculosis. So why is it still so prevalent? This disease preys upon the marginalized, undernourished, and immunocompromised.

item.title: In response to William Perry's 'Some Thoughts About Spring,' some songs from the Great American Songbook about spring - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Instead of celebrating spring, "Spring is Here" and "Spring Can Really Hang You Up The Most" bemoan the coming of spring.

item.title: Why are Arthur Batacchi and Kimberly Alcantara still on the Southern Berkshire Regional School Committee? - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: The time has come to get some new people on the School Committee.

item.title: FILM REVIEW: Huo Meng's 'Living the Land' opens at the Film Forum on April 3 - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: The film, which is a bit too leisurely, is less focused on individual character than on community and extended family—forces that, alongside a distant and repressive government, define their lives.

item.title: BITS &amp;amp; BYTES: Better Than Ezra at The Mahaiwe; ‘A Doll's House Part 2,’ at Bennington Theater; Natalie Hamilton at American Mural Project; North Adams Pride Northern Lights Ball; Becket Arts Center Novel Creations Ball; OLLI and BCHS present Cynthia Farr Brown; Bidwell House presents Donald F. Johnson; Jewish Federation presents Andrew Porwancher; Open Mic at First Congregational Church of GB - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Named one of the “100 Greatest Alternative Artists of All Time” by Billboard, Better Than Ezra has made their mark on the music world.

item.title: Notes from Southern Berkshire Ambulance: April 2026 - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Well, it’s been a month and we’ve been busy. Call volume was up, with approximately 250 calls. Thanks to our team for keeping South County safe!

item.title: Ted Portnoff, 93, of Great Barrington - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Calling hours will be held on Saturday, April 18, from 1 to 3 p.m. at Finnerty & Stevens Funeral Home. A graveside service will follow at Elmwood Cemetery.

item.title: Great Barrington Selectboard reviews proposed draft of Trust Policy revision - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: A proposed revision to the town's 2017 Trust Policy would expand it from two pages to seven, focusing on greater clarity and transparency and adding new pillars addressing police accountability, immigration enforcement boundaries, and community outreach.

item.title: Berkshire District Attorney Shugrue clears Hinsdale police officer in Jan. 7 fatal shooting - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: “While the findings were non-criminal, I find it imperative to state that while there will be no criminal charges, the Force Investigation Team did find considerable concern regarding policies in the Hinsdale Police Department," said District Attorney Shugrue.

item.title: For the love of books! Berkshire Book Con to be held at Pittsfield’s Berkshire Athenaeum, Hot Plate Brewing Co., April 18 - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: The day’s events include an author talk and book signing with author Shelly Jay Shore, a behind-the-scenes look at some of the processes that go into making a book, and a book fair and social hour, organized and hosted by Indie Readery & Records and Hot Plate Brewing Co.

item.title: PREVIEW: Eugene Drucker & Friends to give concert Sunday, April 19, to benefit Stockbridge Library Museum and Archives - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Top-tier chamber musicians join Eugene Drucker for a benefit concert featuring Beethoven, Brahms, and a new work by Drucker.

item.title: Music magic with Derek Wang - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Derek Wang first performed his "Magic Piano" and "The Chopin Shorts" in a children’s film festival at Lincoln Center when he was 12 years old! But what followed was as enchanting for adults as for children.

item.title: Pittsfield CityJazz Festival marks 20 years with 'Women in Jazz' theme April 17 through 25 - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Nine-day festival features Georgia Heers, Grace Kelly, and Veronica Swift, along with a jazz crawl, jam session, and youth showcase across Pittsfield.

item.title: STEPHEN COHEN: Faith and hypocrisy - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Why can so many devoutly religious individuals support such hatred of others, based solely on religion, culture, politics, and their location.

item.title: BITS & BYTES April 14, 2026: What’s happening in the Berkshires and beyond! - The Berkshire Edge
item.description: Announcements from Berkshires Jazz, The Mahaiwe, Kaatsbaan, The Foundry, Drag Story Hour Berkshires, and more!
